reader_contrast: The man of God originally declared the message, while the current speaker says that it will come true.
reader_reason: The window supports the intended answer through the antecedent of “he,” but the question blurs the original declarer with the current speaker. Asking who originally declared the message would recover the intended relation.
editor_quote: the man of God is buried; lay my bones beside his bones. For the message he declared by the word of the Lord against the altar in Bethel and against all the shrines on the high places in the towns of Samaria will certainly come true.
editor_contrast: The man of God originally declared the message, whereas the speaker tells his sons that it will come true.
editor_reason: The speaker is a plausible answer because he is the one now saying the message will come true. The generic verb “gives” and the pronoun “he” blur that role with the man of God’s role as the original declarer. Asking who originally declared the message would make the key unique.

question: Who mounts the donkey?

reader_reason: The singular “he” refers to the old prophet who requested the donkey; the sons are the plural “they” who saddle it.
editor_quote: So he said to his sons, “Saddle the donkey for me.” And when they had saddled the donkey for him, he mounted it
editor_contrast: The sons saddle the donkey, but their father, the old prophet, mounts it.
editor_reason: The change from “they” to “he” distinguishes the sons who prepare the donkey from the old prophet who rides it.

reader_reason: The pronoun “he” refers to the immediately named son, Josiah, and sacrificing the priests entails killing them.
editor_quote: A son named Josiah will be born to the house of David. On you he will sacrifice the priests of the high places who make offerings here
editor_contrast: The future son Josiah is the actor in the prophecy, not Jeroboam, who is merely standing by the altar when it is announced.
editor_reason: Jeroboam is a plausible misreading because he is present at the altar, but the prophecy introduces Josiah and then says that “he” will sacrifice the priests. In this context, sacrificing them entails killing them.

question: Whose body is warned will not be buried with family?

editor_reason: The old prophet could be confused with the person threatened because the word first comes to him. However, he addresses the man of God from Judah, so the second-person phrase “your body” refers to that man.

question: Whom does the king order others to capture?

editor_contrast: Jeroboam gives the order, while the man of God is the person the order targets.
editor_reason: The king is the speaker and points toward the man of God when ordering others to seize “him,” resolving the pronoun’s reference.

question: Why does the man of God refuse the king’s offer?

reader_contrast: The Lord’s command causes the refusal; the offer of half the king’s possessions is a hypothetical concession, not the reason.
reader_reason: “For” introduces the man’s stated reason, while “even if” shows that a larger offer would not change his refusal. The question tests that causal and concessive relationship.
editor_quote: For I was commanded by the word of the Lord
editor_contrast: The Lord’s command is the reason for the refusal; the amount of the king’s offer is only part of a rejected hypothetical.
editor_reason: The man of God explicitly introduces the Lord’s command as his reason. Saying “even if” the king offered half his possessions rules out the offer’s size as the cause.

reader_reason: In the alleged angelic message, “him” and “he” refer to the man of God. However, “According to the claim” is an avoidably generic reference and should identify the old prophet’s alleged message.
editor_quote: So the man of God returned with him and ate and drank in his house.
editor_contrast: The man of God as the intended eater and drinker versus the old prophet who reports the claim.
editor_reason: The old prophet is plausible because he voices the claim and owns the house, but the third-person “him” and “he” refer to the person he is addressing. The following action confirms that this is the man of God.

reader_contrast: The king requests prayer, while the man of God performs it.
